title: Kummer branch classification
statement: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] with fraction field $F$ [def-pc-field-extension] of characteristic zero and residue characteristic a prime $p$. Let $\zeta\in R$ have multiplicative order $p$, put $w=1-\zeta$, and put $P(T)=((1+wT)^p-1)/w^p$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Normalize the integer valuation $v$ by $v(t)=1$ for a uniformizer $t$, and set $v(0)=+\infty$. For $\eta\in F$ with $w^p\eta\in\mathfrak m_R$, the algebra $D=F[T]/(P(T)-\eta)$ is either $F^p$ or a cyclic Galois field extension $E/F$ of degree $p$. In the field case its integral closure $S$ of $R$ is a complete DVR. The possibilities are ramification index $p$ with unchanged residue field, or ramification index one with residue extension either separable of degree $p$ or purely inseparable of degree $p$. Ramification index $a$ means $\mathfrak m_RS=\mathfrak m_S^a$, purely inseparable of degree $p$ means degree $p$ and every residue element has its $p$th power in the base residue field, and cyclic Galois means a normal separable extension with cyclic automorphism group [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. More precisely: if $\eta\in R$, every normalized factor of $D$ has ramification index one over $R$; if $v(\eta)=-d<0$ with $p\nmid d$, then $D$ is a degree-$p$ totally ramified field extension; if $v(\eta)=-d<0$ with $p\mid d$ and the residue of $t^d\eta$ is not a $p$th power, then $D$ is a degree-$p$ field extension with ramification index one and purely inseparable residue extension of degree $p$. The normalization of $R$ in the split algebra $F^p$ is $R^p$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Finite means finite-dimensional, and totally ramified means unchanged residue field and ramification index equal to the field degree.

source.place: Tag 09F3, lemma-extension-defined-by-nice-polynial, cases (A)-(C), restricted to finite-level parameters; Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension (complete normalization). Normalized tensor algebras as in Tag 09EM, remark-construction.

proof.text: Write $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, $h=v(w)>0$. By [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus], $P\in R[T]$ is monic of degree $p$ and $P(T)=T^p-T+\sum_{1\le i<p}a_iT^i$ with $a_i\in wR$. The finite-level assumption makes $b=1+w^p\eta$ a unit of $R$, hence nonzero. The invertible affine substitutions $Y=1+wT$ and $T=(Y-1)/w$ give $D\cong F[Y]/(Y^p-b)$: explicitly $Y^p-b=w^p(P(T)-\eta)$. This is the Kummer equation used below; the source's printed $y^p=w^p(1+\xi)$ is not this equation.

source.place: Tag 09F3, lemma-extension-defined-by-nice-polynial, first proof paragraph; Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare

proof.text: The $p$ distinct powers of $\zeta$ exhaust the roots of $X^p-1$. By [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], choose an algebraic closure; by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], the nonconstant polynomial $Y^p-b$ has a root $y$ there, and put $E=F(y)$. Apply [lem-sfb-multiradical-galois-degree] with $n=p,r=1,a_1=b$: $E/F$ is finite Galois and $[E:F]\mid p$, hence its degree is $1$ or $p$. By [lem-sfb-split-binomial-root-torsor], all roots are the distinct $y\zeta^j$. If the degree is $1$, they lie in $F$; their linear ideals are pairwise coprime, and [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] gives $D\cong F^p$. If the degree is $p$, evaluation $F[Y]/(Y^p-b)\to E$ is surjective: its image is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], and contains $F,y$. The source and target both have dimension $p$, the source by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], so evaluation is an isomorphism. Thus $Y^p-b$ is irreducible, and $E$ is its splitting field by the displayed roots. Apply [lem-exc-kummer-binomial-splitting-field] to get the cyclic Galois assertion.

source.place: Tag 09F3, first proof paragraph; Fields Tag 09I6, section-Kummer, opening paragraph

proof.text: In the field case [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization] gives the finite complete DVR $S\subset E$, with fraction field $E$ and local inclusion $R\to S$. There is only one maximal ideal of $S$. Apply [lem-exc-dvr-galois-degree-data] to the degree-$p$ Galois extension $E/F$: its formula $[E:F]=gef$ has $g=1$, so $p=af$, where $a$ is the ramification index and $f=[\kappa_S:k]$. Since $a,f$ are positive integers, either $(a,f)=(p,1)$, which is total ramification, or $(a,f)=(1,p)$.

source.place: Tag 09E8, remark-finite-separable-extension; Tag 09F3, first proof paragraph

proof.text: For any extension $l/k$ of degree $p$ in characteristic $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] gives $k\subset l_s\subset l$ with $l_s/k$ separable and $l/l_s$ purely inseparable. The tower formula [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] gives $p=[l:l_s][l_s:k]$, so $l_s=l$ or $l_s=k$. In the first case $l/k$ is separable. In the second it is purely inseparable of degree $p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-pth-root-tower] in this second case: its tower consists of degree-$p$ steps, so the same degree formula forces exactly one step. Thus $l=k(\alpha)$ with $\alpha^p\in k$. Every element is a linear combination of $1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{p-1}$, and the characteristic-$p$ power identity shows its $p$th power lies in $k$. Applying this to $l=\kappa_S$ completes the general classification.

source.place: Tag 09F3, first proof paragraph; Fields Tags 030K (lemma-separable-first), 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable), 09G9 (lemma-multiplicativity-degrees)

proof.text: Suppose $\eta\in R$ and put $B=R[T]/(P-\eta)$. It is finite free by [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. Its polynomial derivative is $-1$ modulo $tB$: the coefficients $a_i$ lie in $wR\subset tR$ and $p\in tR$. The unit form of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] therefore makes the derivative invertible in $B$. Thus $B$ equals its localization at the derivative, so [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] makes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ finite etale. The base $R$ is Noetherian and normal by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. By [lem-sfb-finite-etale-normal-generic-components], each generic field factor of $D$ has normalization a finite etale component over $R$. That normalization has a unique closed point by [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization] (also for a factor equal to $F$). Its local ring is the normalization itself, and [lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk] says its maximal ideal is generated by the image of $t$. Hence every normalized factor has ramification index one, as asserted in case (A).

Suppose $v(\eta)=-d<0$. In a normalized field factor let $z$ be the image of $T$, and write $
u$ for its integer valuation, with $
u(t)=a$. This includes the split case, where the factors are $F$ and $a=1$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] to a numerator and denominator of $c\in F^	imes$: $c=u t^{v(c)}$ for a unit $u\in R^	imes$. Hence $
u(c)=av(c)$ for $c\in F^	imes$: a unit of $R$ stays a unit in the local extension, since its inverse is still in $R$. Since $P$ has integral coefficients, $
u(z)\ge0$ would imply $
u(P(z))\ge0$, contradicting $
u(\eta)=-ad$. Thus $q=
u(z)<0$. Every term of $P(z)$ of degree $i<p$ has valuation at least $iq>pq$, while the monic leading term has valuation $pq$. The unique term of least valuation cannot cancel (divide the sum by that term; the other summands lie in the maximal ideal, so the quotient is a unit). Consequently $p
u(z)=-ad$.

source.place: Tag 09F3, case (B), valuation equality; polynomial form supplied in Step 1

proof.text: If $p\nmid d$, the equation $p\nu(z)=-ad$ forces $p\mid a$. A split factor would have $a=1$, which is impossible. Thus $D$ is the degree-$p$ field of Step 2. In Step 3, $af=p$, and $p\mid a$ now forces $a=p,f=1$. This is precisely case (B).

Suppose $d=pm>0$ and put $u=t^d\eta\in R^\times$, with $\bar u\notin k^p$. Scaling $U=t^mT$ gives the monic polynomial
$$Q(U)=U^p-t^{d-m}U+\sum_{1\le i<p}a_i t^{d-im}U^i-u.$$
Indeed $Q(t^mT)=t^d(P(T)-\eta)$. Since $d-im=(p-i)m>0$, all nonleading, nonconstant coefficients lie in $tR$, so $\bar Q=U^p-\bar u$. By [lem-weil-pbc-x-pow-p-minus-t-irreducible] this reduction is irreducible, and by [lem-trf-irreducible-polynomial-quotient-field] its quotient is a field. Now [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] makes $C=R[U]/(Q)$ finite free of rank $p$ with that field as $C/tC$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-free-field-fibre-dvr]: $C$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $tC$. Its generic algebra is $D$ by the displayed substitution. Since $C$ is a domain, its finite-dimensional generic algebra is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], and its fraction field equals this generic algebra. Thus Step 2 forces $[D:F]=p$. The local inclusion $R\to C$ and the uniqueness clause of [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization] identify $C=S$. Consequently $S$ is complete, $a=1$, and its residue field is $k[U]/(U^p-\bar u)$ of degree $p$.

source.place: Tag 09F3, case (C), scaled monic quotient; Fields Tag 09HF, lemma-take-pth-root; Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr

proof.text: In the last residue field, write an arbitrary element as $\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}c_i\bar U^i$. Its $p$th power is $\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}c_i^p\bar u^i\in k$, since the intermediate binomial coefficients vanish in characteristic $p$. This is the stated purely inseparable condition in case (C). Finally, in the split case a tuple in $F^p$ integral over $R$ has each coordinate integral over $R$, by evaluating its monic equation coordinatewise. Each coordinate then lies in $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Conversely a tuple $(r_j)\in R^p$ is annihilated by the monic polynomial $\prod_j(X-r_j)$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], the normalization in $F^p$ is therefore exactly $R^p$.
